sample_unit: pathologists compared against the AI grading (test cohorts: 320 annotated slides; 3 pathologists in the assisted-reading study)
models_evaluated: convolutional neural network for tumour and regression tissue detection (11 tissue classes)

links.outcome: Pathologist performance with versus without AI assistance: interobserver agreement and diagnostic time
links.effect: Use of the AI tool by three pathologists increased interobserver agreement and substantially reduced diagnostic time per case compared with working without AI assistance. Overreliance was not reported.
links.quote: Use of the AI tool by three pathologists increased interobserver agreement and substantially reduced diagnostic time per case compared with working without AI assistance.

links.outcome: AI regression grading compared against a group of 12 pathologists on the same retrospective cases
links.effect: Case-level agreement was 63·6% (quadratic kappa 0·749). AI grading triggered true reclassification in seven cases, six of which had small tumour regions initially missed by pathologists.
links.quote: The AI-based regression grading triggered true reclassification of resected tumour slides in seven cases (including six cases who had small tumour regions that were initially missed by pathologists).

links.outcome: Patch-level accuracy on independent external test cohorts from multiple institutions
links.effect: In four independent test cohorts from three institutes and TCGA, the AI tool had high patch-level accuracy for identifying tumour and regression tissue.
links.quote: In the independent test cohorts the AI tool had high patch-level accuracy for identifying both tumour and regression tissue.

screen.reason: The study conducts a reader study comparing pathologists' performance, interobserver agreement, and assessment time with versus without AI assistance.
